summary: Conor Roddy is a philosopher who earned a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (~2005–2011), where Stephen H. Phillips served on his committee. He also studied under teachers Arindam Chakrabarti and Roger T. Ames.

Constance E. Kassor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After completing a BA at Smith College under Jay L. Garfield, she earned a PhD at Emory University (~2007–2014) supervised by John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later joining Smith's faculty (~2013–2014).

Constance Powell Chin works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed a master's degree at San Jose State University (~2009–2012) supervised by John W. Bernhardt, with Jonathan P. Roth and Christian Jochim on her committee, and studied under Christian Luczanits.

Constantin Regamey (1907–1982) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Warsaw and Paris under Stanisław Schayer, Jean Przyluski, and Marcelle Lalou. He taught at Warsaw (~1936–1941) and became a professor at Lausanne and Fribourg in 1944.

Cornelis Jan Kuiken specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Groningen (~1997–2002) under the supervision of Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer, having also studied under MA supervisor Jaap den Hollander.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1848–1853) and served as Professor of the History of Religions at Leiden University from around 1877 to 1900.

Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome.
Cortland Dahl works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and received mentorship from Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

Craig J. Reynolds (born 1941) is a scholar of history/archaeology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Amherst College (~1959–1963) and Cornell University (~1967–1973), he held a post at the Australian National University around 1989.

Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has served as a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge, and as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection at the University of Cambridge.
Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia, where he was taught by Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson (1981–1985).

Cristina Pecchia works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Sapienza University (PhD ~1999–2003) under Gnoli, Torella, and Pensa, and at Vienna in 2000 under Steinkellner, becoming a project researcher at IKGA around 2007.

Cristina Scherrer-Schaub (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She has held posts as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1999–2012), directeur d'études at the EPHE (~2000–2015), and professor at the Collège de France.

Csaba Dezső (born 1973) is an Indologist who earned master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University (~1991–1998) and a PhD at Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. He served as Assistant Lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University from 2004 to 2016.

Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts as a research assistant at Eötvös Loránd University (~2006–2009) and at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2014–2017).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held a post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2014–2015) and became Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Toronto around 2017.

Culadasa (1944–2021) worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having studied under traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu. He served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha from around 2008 to 2019.

Cuma Ozkan works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa (~2011–2013) under supervisor Morten Schlütter, with Melissa Anne-Marie Curley and Frederick M. Smith on his committee.

Cuong T. Mai specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. After an MA at Hawaii, he earned a PhD at Indiana University (~2001–2009) under John R. McRae, later serving as an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel works in history/archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by John M. Rosenfield and having studied under Keizaburō Mizuno, she held a post at the University of Washington from around 2002 to 2012.
